extracted.intended_audience: CHI 2024 paper reviewers (program committee, external reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewing and recommending decisions on submissions to the CHI 2024 conference, focusing on whether a paper provides a strong contribution to HCI and on review quality and procedural policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Evaluation Criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does this submission provide a strong contribution to the field of HCI?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the fundamental standard; reviewers must assess contribution strength contextually because contributions can appear via diverse pathways rather than via a single rigid template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution types (acceptable forms of contribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists contribution categories the conference recognizes: empirical studies; design contributions; theoretical frameworks; methodological contributions; replications; dataset contributions; survey/integration contributions; opinion/argument contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate papers according to the norms of the contribution type presented. The guide emphasizes that diverse forms of contribution qualify as legitimate CHI contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication valued
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive replications with sufficient information represent legitimate contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replication work is accepted provided it is constructive and reported with enough detail to be useful; do not dismiss replications by default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original research required
rubrics_metrics.description: All CHI papers must advance knowledge in human-computer interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should present new insights, findings, methods, or syntheses that move HCI knowledge forward; mere re-reporting of known results without added value is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Doubt about contributions grows when research reporting lacks transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess transparency of methods, data, analyses, and reporting. Lack of transparency weakens perceived contribution and can reduce confidence in results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers should match length to contribution scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper length must be appropriate for the depth and scope of the contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider whether the chosen paper length (short vs long) is commensurate with what the paper claims to contribute; mismatched length is a ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short papers length expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Short papers (<5,000 words): brief, focused contributions; do not demand comprehensiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short submissions can be valuable for focused ideas or preliminary results; reviewers should not penalize short papers for not being comprehensive as long as the contribution matches the format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long papers length expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Long papers (7,000–8,000 words): substantial depth and results are expected and should be justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long papers should provide sufficient depth, methodological detail, and results appropriate to their extended length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive length policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive length (>12,000 words) requires author justification and faces additional scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must justify very long submissions; reviewers should apply extra scrutiny to ensure the additional length is warranted by the contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length-commensurability critical standard
rubrics_metrics.description: "Papers whose lengths are incommensurate with their contributions will be rejected."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A central enforceable rule: if a paper's length is not justified by the significance or scope of its contribution, reviewers should recommend rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review detail minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should provide detailed feedback: approximately one page minimum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short reviews lack constructive value; aim for at least one page of substantive comments including evidence and examples to support assessments and suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justified assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Both positive and negative reviews require substantive argumentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations must be supported by clear reasoning and evidence (e.g., pointing to manuscript sections, methodological issues, or results) rather than unsupported opinions or single-line statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer accuracy responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers own their content, including citation accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims in reviews (including citations of prior work) are accurate; reviewers are responsible for the factual correctness of their comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality protection (including LLM risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid sharing unpublished work with online tools; LLMs pose confidentiality risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect authors' unpublished content; do not paste submission text or confidential reviewer comments into external services that could leak content or violate confidentiality (language models included).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted recommendation labels: Accept with minor revisions; Revise and Resubmit; Reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these categories to communicate decision and expected next steps. Reviews should align their justification and requested changes with the chosen recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcommittee-fit non-penalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not judge the paper by how well it fits the subcommittee theme(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many papers do not cleanly fit a subcommittee; reviewers must evaluate merit independent of thematic alignment and avoid penalizing papers for lack of fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior publication / prior material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously published material requires "more than 25% of new content material" for republication; non-archival venues (workshops, posters, late-breaking work) do not count as prior publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for overlap with prior publications; if substantial prior material exists, ensure the submission adds >25% new content to be eligible. Treat workshop/poster/non-archival versions as not precluding submission.
